transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 mins
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Avery Brooks (Cedarfall HO ML), Jordan Lee (Infra), Riley Carter (CISO), Sam Dunn (Product)

Summary: discovery focused on Dedicated capacity needs for Cedarfall's inference workloads; discussed reserved GPUs, isolation and VPC needs, burst/fallback to hosted, scaling expectations and POC plan. Security and compliance requirements reviewed (SOC2, KMS, audit logs).

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. just to set context, we're here to talk about dedicated capacity options and how we can support cedarfall's latency and data isolation needs. tiny intro round?
[00:12] Avery (Cedarfall): hey, avery here, head of ml. we're evaluating dedicated reserved gpus because we need predictable throughput for our realtime scoring, and we have some data residency constraints.
[00:22] Jordan (Cedarfall): jordan, infra. we'll run the cluster in our VPC, want to understand networking and burst patterns.
[00:28] Riley (Cedarfall): riley, security - SOC2 background, KMS integration questions.
[00:33] Maya: great. ethan is our se who will dig into sizing. ethan?
[00:37] Ethan (Redwood): hi all, quick outline: we usually size based on tokens per second, simult connections, and sequence length. we'll talk instance types (A100/H100) and quantization options (int8), plus autoscale and burst to hosted if you need extra capacity.

[01:05] Avery: a couple of facts: our baseline is about 6k QPS at peak for small prompt generation across multiple models, avg seq length ~128 tokens, but we have some long-running batch jobs that go up to 2k tokens. uptime SLO is 99.95 and p95 latency target under 250ms for the realtime model.

[01:35] Ethan: okay, that helps. for 6k QPS at ~128 tokens, depending on model size we recommend reserved pool w/ dedicated gpu nodes. do you have a prefered model family - open Llama, gpt-style, or a mixed fleet?

[01:48] Avery: we run a mix - majority is a fine-tuned open-llama variant and a smaller number of calls to a 70B for high-quality responses. we'd like to pin versions for rollouts.

[02:05] Jordan: question on isolation - we need VPC private deployment, but still want Redwood to manage the control plane. is that Private option, or does Dedicated support customer VPC peering?

[02:18] Maya: good question. Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools in a tenant-isolated environment; for fully private control plane with customer-managed networking that's Redwood Private. however we can support VPC peering and private networking for Dedicated in many cases - we'll map exact options in the proposal.

[02:45] Riley: for compliance: we need KMS/HSM integration, audit logs retention for 1 year, SSO/SAML, and data at rest encryption. is that supported on Dedicated?

[02:58] Ethan: yes, we support KMS integrations for key wrapping on duty, audit logs and SSO. sometimes the terminology in our docs comes out as "K V cash" in transcriptions, but it's KV cache - for caching. logs retention is configurable as an add-on.

[03:20] Sam (Cedarfall): quick one on failure modes - if you lose a node or an entire AZ, what's the failover and capacity fallback?

[03:28] Ethan: Dedicated pools are distributed across AZs where possible; we offer autoscaling and burst-to-hosted fallback so during extreme spikes we can route requests to compatible hosted model variants automatically. there is a tradeoff: cost and data routing. fallback can be restricted per policy.

[03:50] Avery: curious about warm vs cold KV cache effects on latency, our p95 is tight.

[03:55] Ethan: warm KV cache is critical. we do prefix/KV caching; for heavy prefix reuse you'll see large latency wins. we'll set up tests to measure cold start and warm steady-state; expectation is cold p95 higher initially but warm p95 should be within your 250ms target depending on model and batching.

[04:30] [Speaker 1]: (murmur) how about quantization?

[04:33] Ethan: int8 quantization can reduce memory and improve throughput, often with minimal quality regression. for your 70B variant we can evaluate int8+AWQ or similar profiles during the POC.

[05:00] Jordan: about autoscale - do you offer instant scale up or is there scale lag? we need to design for flash traffic, like sudden market events.

[05:09] Maya: we expose autoscale policies and burst capacity. typical scale-up has small lag depending on instance availability, but burst-to-hosted gives near-instant capacity by routing to pre-warmed hosted clusters or smaller model variants. we'll quantify expected cold-start latencies in the POC.

[05:35] Riley: network egress - we need to ensure logs and telemetry don't leave region. can you run everything in-region?

[05:43] Ethan: yes, we can pin region and keep logs within region; for Dedicated with VPC peering you can also route logs to your own SIEM.

[06:00] Avery: another operational question: how do you handle model rollouts and canarying with dedicated pools? we don't want a bad model push to affect all traffic.

[06:10] Ethan: Redwood supports canary deployments and route-based rollouts; with Dedicated you can pin versions per route and do traffic splits. fallback policies allow automatic switch back to previous model if metrics degrade.

[06:36] Maya: can we talk numbers - what's a realistic node count?

[06:40] Ethan: rough ballpark - for your workload: 70B for high-quality responses might need 8-12 H100-like GPUs to hit latency targets at peak if no quantization; open-llama 13B or 33B variants could be served on A100 or quantized smaller footprints. overall you'd likely reserve a mixed pool: a few H100 nodes for the 70B and larger count of A100/int8 nodes for the 13/33B family. we'll refine after we see exact concurrency and batching profile.

[07:10] Jordan: pricing question - per-hour per-GPU or committed monthly?

[07:14] Maya: Dedicated is typically committed capacity (monthly/annual) with a fixed SKU mix; we can model monthly cost and show examples with burst-to-hosted add-on.

[07:30] Sam: benchmarks - can you run p99/p95 tests against our traffic shape?

[07:35] Ethan: yes, POC will include benchmark harness: your traffic replay, cold/warm cache runs, latency percentiles, and token throughput metrics. we'll share the harness and results spreadsheet.

[08:00] Riley: security again: do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) in KMS? and hardware security module (HSM)?

[08:10] Ethan: yes, CMK via customer KMS is available on Private; on Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS in many deployments - HSM availability depends on region and deployment model; we'll call that out.

[08:35] Avery: what about maintenance windows and patching? we need predictable windows and advance notice.

[08:41] Maya: we give scheduled maintenance windows, canary updates, and advance notice. for Dedicated we align with customers to minimize impact.

[09:00] Jordan: on-networking: do you support private ENIs and no-public-ip for nodes?

[09:06] Ethan: yes, private networking, ENI support and VPC peering are supported. we'll include a network diagram in the follow-up.

[09:25] [cross talk]

[09:30] Maya: quick pause - any blockers from your side for moving to a POC?

[09:35] Avery: we need to validate costs and get security signoff; once we have a pricing model and a compliance checklist we'll be good.

[09:45] Riley: also want to see audit log format and retention controls.

[10:00] Ethan: we'll include sample audit logs and retention configs.

[10:15] Avery: what about model licensing and IPR for fine-tuning? we fine-tuned internal models.

[10:22] Maya: Redwood doesn't take model ownership; you retain models. we provide serving and infra. licensing depends on underlying model license - we'll annotate in the doc.

[10:40] Jordan: curious about fallback policies - can we force fallback to an on-premise cluster if cloud region unavailable?

[10:46] Ethan: yes, you can define routing policies: latency-first or isolation-first. cross-region and on-prem fallbacks require setup but are supported in Private or hybrid setups.

[11:05] Sam: SLA questions - is 99.95 backed by credits or financial SLA?

[11:10] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA tiers; we'll include the SLA options in the proposal.

[11:25] Avery: okay, timeline: we want to start POC in ~2 weeks and run 2-3 weeks of benchmarking. is that feasible?

[11:32] Ethan: yes, we can do a 2-3 week POC, need a couple days to prepare infra and warm models; we'll provide a checklist of what we need from you.

[11:50] Riley: any red flags around data residency? we must ensure no backups leave region.

[11:56] Ethan: noted - we'll include retention and region pinning options and confirm backup policies in writing.

[12:10] Maya: i'll recap next steps at the end but ethan will own the POC plan.

[12:18] Ethan: next steps recap - I'll produce: POC scope, test harness, instance mix suggestion, metrics to collect, and a runbook for canary/rollback.

[12:35] Avery: for throughput numbers, we'll share a 7-day histogram of QPS and seq length.

[12:45] Jordan: i'll export infra diagrams and current network egress policy.

[12:55] Riley: i'll circulate the compliance checklist items we need Redwood to confirm.

[13:05] Maya: perfect. any final quick Qs?

[13:10] Sam: one more - can you show example cost math for reserved vs hosted?

[13:16] Maya: yes, we'll include cost comparisons (committed monthly vs burst and pay-as-you-go hosted) in the pricing doc.

[13:30] Wrap-up:
Maya: thanks everyone, we'll send the pricing and POC plan and set up the kickoff.
Avery: thanks, talk soon.
[13:42] call ends

Notes and artifacts referenced:
